project: Vibey Machine — Per-User Docker on Fly.io
description: Containerize OpenClaw (Vibey agent only) + agent-api into a Docker image with a custom tool plugin that routes all agent actions through the backend. Deploy on Fly.io with one machine per user, provisioned at signup. Staging on Hetzner VM, production on Fly.io.

context.currentProblem: Vibey agent + agent-api + OpenClaw gateway run on a single shared Hetzner VM. All users share the same instance. The agent currently uses 'exec curl' to call Supabase Edge Functions directly, bypassing the backend. No per-user isolation, no Docker, no Fly.io.
context.desiredState: Each user gets their own isolated Docker container on Fly.io containing OpenClaw (Vibey agent only) + agent-api. The agent uses a custom tool plugin (vibey_backend) to route all actions through the backend. Agent cannot write files, exec commands, or access the DB directly. All user creations (offers, funnels, emails, lead magnets) are stored in the shared Supabase database via the backend. Credentials are encrypted in DB, agent sees capability list only.
context.architectureGoal: VM vs DB split: agent consciousness files (SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, skills) are read-only on the VM/container. All user creations go to the database via agent-api backend. Backend proxies all external API calls. Agent never sees raw credentials. Frontend routes chat requests to user's specific Fly.io machine URL.

userStories.title: Build custom OpenClaw tool plugin (vibey-backend)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a custom OpenClaw tool plugin named 'vibey_backend' that the Vibey agent can call to perform CRUD operations on artifacts (offers, funnels, etc.) by routing requests to the local agent-api backend at localhost:3003.
acceptanceCriteria: Directory docker/tools/vibey-backend/ exists with the correct OpenClaw tool plugin structure (refer to OpenClaw tool/plugin docs for required files)
Tool is named 'vibey_backend' (matches the allow list in openclaw.json from US-002)
Tool accepts two parameters: 'action' (string, required) and 'data' (object, optional)
Tool makes HTTP POST requests to http://localhost:3003/api/artifacts with JSON body { action, data }
Tool passes the following headers on every request: Content-Type: application/json, x-openclaw-internal: true (for backend to identify agent requests vs user requests)
Tool returns the JSON response body from the backend to the agent
Tool handles HTTP errors gracefully: if backend returns 4xx/5xx, tool returns a human-readable error message to the agent (NOT raw HTTP error)
Tool handles network errors gracefully: if localhost:3003 is unreachable, tool returns 'Backend is not available, please try again' (not a stack trace)

Supported actions documented in tool description/schema (for the agent to know what's available): create_offer, update_offer_step, get_offer, list_offers, create_funnel, add_funnel_page, list_funnels, create_lead_magnet, list_lead_magnets, create_sequence, add_sequence_email, list_sequences, create_avatar, list_avatars, create_theme, list_themes, save_document, list_documents, get_capabilities, use_integration
Tool does NOT expose any URLs, tokens, or internal details to the agent — the agent only sees the action name and response data
Tool is registered in openclaw.json or in the correct OpenClaw tools directory so it loads automatically on gateway boot
TypeScript compiles without errors (if tool is TypeScript; otherwise tool works when tested manually)
userStories.notes: IMPORTANT: Research OpenClaw custom tool/plugin documentation first. The exact plugin structure, manifest format, and registration method must be verified from OpenClaw docs (https://docs.openclaw.ai). Do NOT guess the structure. If OpenClaw tools are JavaScript/TypeScript files, follow their exact pattern. If they're Python scripts, follow that. The tool runs inside the Docker container where both OpenClaw and agent-api are on localhost.

userStories.title: Build artifacts CRUD module in agent-api backend
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a new NestJS module in agent-api that handles all artifact CRUD operations (offers, funnels, lead magnets, emails, avatars, themes, documents) through a single action-based endpoint, following the 3-layer architecture.
acceptanceCriteria: New module at apps/agent-api/src/modules/artifacts/ with standard structure: controllers/, services/, dtos/
artifacts.module.ts registered in app.module.ts imports array
artifacts.controller.ts: POST /api/artifacts endpoint that accepts { action: string, data: object }
Controller uses an internal auth guard that validates x-openclaw-internal header (agent requests from localhost) — NOT the standard user JWT AuthGuard
Controller uses @UseGuards(ThrottlerGuard) with appropriate rate limits
Controller delegates to artifacts.service.ts — NO business logic in controller
Controller file stays under 200 LOC per backend-architecture.md
artifacts.service.ts: action router that maps action strings to handler methods

Service supports ALL actions from the plan: create_offer, update_offer_step, get_offer, list_offers, create_funnel, add_funnel_page, list_funnels, create_lead_magnet, list_lead_magnets, create_sequence, add_sequence_email, list_sequences, create_avatar, list_avatars, create_theme, list_themes, save_document, list_documents
Service reads USER_ID from environment variable (injected per container) — NOT from request body or JWT
Service uses Supabase client with service role key (since agent-api acts on behalf of the user, the user ID is injected as env var, and RLS is not applicable in this context)
Service implements error logging with LoggerService: all DB errors logged with feature 'artifacts/{action}', error_code 'DB_ERROR'
Service file stays under 600 LOC — if larger, split into sub-services (offer-artifacts.service.ts, funnel-artifacts.service.ts, etc.)
Zod DTOs defined in dtos/ for each action's data payload (e.g., CreateOfferDto, UpdateOfferStepDto, CreateFunnelDto, etc.)
Input validated with ZodValidationPipe before processing
Error responses sanitized — no internal DB details returned to agent
Successful responses return { success: true, data: {...} }
Error responses return { success: false, error: 'Human-readable message' }
TypeScript compiles without errors
Module follows code-guidelines-backend.md: constructor injection, single responsibility, proper error handling
userStories.notes: CRITICAL: Read the existing openclaw-proxy.service.ts and chat.service.ts in apps/agent-api/src/modules/chat/ to understand how the agent-api currently works. The artifacts module is a NEW module alongside chat, not a replacement. The current Supabase Edge Function (vibey-artifacts) handles these actions — port the logic to NestJS, don't rewrite from scratch. Reference the current Edge Function's action handling for the exact Supabase queries needed. The service role key is acceptable here because the agent-api is the trusted backend acting on behalf of a known user (USER_ID from env).

userStories.title: Build credential proxy module in agent-api backend
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a credential proxy module in agent-api that stores encrypted credentials, returns capability lists to the agent, and proxies external API calls so the agent never sees raw API keys.
acceptanceCriteria: New module at apps/agent-api/src/modules/credentials/ with standard structure: controllers/, services/, dtos/
credentials.module.ts registered in app.module.ts imports array
GET /api/capabilities endpoint: returns a list of available integrations and their capabilities for the current user (reads from credentials table where user_id matches env USER_ID and revoked=false)
Response format: { capabilities: [{ service: 'shopify', actions: ['read_products', 'write_products'] }, ...] }
POST /api/integrations/execute endpoint: accepts { service: string, action: string, params: object }, decrypts the credential for that service, makes the external API call, and returns the result
Credentials stored in Supabase with AES-256 encryption (encrypted_value column). Backend decrypts using ENCRYPTION_KEY env var.
Every credential usage logged in credential_usage table: credential_id, agent_id, action, params (sanitized), response_status, created_at
Agent NEVER receives raw API keys/tokens — only the capability list and action results
If credential is revoked (revoked=true), return error 'Integration is disabled'
If credential not found, return error 'Integration not available'
Controller uses ThrottlerGuard with strict rate limits (10/min for external API calls)
Service implements error logging with LoggerService
Zod validation on all inputs
TypeScript compiles without errors
File size limits respected (controller <200 LOC, service <600 LOC)
userStories.notes: This is Phase 2 of the PRD (credential architecture). The DB schema for credentials table is defined in .docs/.tasks/vibey_machine/prd.md section 9.1. The encryption/decryption implementation should use Node.js crypto module with AES-256-GCM. ENCRYPTION_KEY is a 32-byte key passed as env var. For Phase 1, this module can be stubbed (return empty capabilities) and fully implemented when users actually need integrations.

acceptanceCriteria: File docker/Dockerfile exists at monorepo root
Multi-stage build: Stage 1 builds agent-api (FROM node:22-bookworm AS api-builder), Stage 2 uses OpenClaw base image (FROM ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:main)

Stage 2: installs supervisord (apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends supervisor)
Stage 2: copies built agent-api (dist + node_modules + package.json) to /app/agent-api/
Stage 2: copies docker/openclaw.json to /home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json
Stage 2: copies docker/agents/vibey/ to /app/agents/vibey/ (read-only workspace)
Stage 2: copies docker/tools/vibey-backend/ to /home/node/.openclaw/tools/vibey-backend/
Stage 2: copies docker/supervisord.conf to /etc/supervisor/conf.d/vibey.conf
EXPOSE 3003 (agent-api port — the only externally accessible port)
CMD runs supervisord in foreground mode
docker/.dockerignore exists and excludes: node_modules, .git, *.log, .env*, dist (from source), __tests__
docker/supervisord.conf exists and configures two processes: openclaw-gateway (command to start OpenClaw gateway) and agent-api (command: node /app/agent-api/dist/main.js, env PORT=3003)
supervisord.conf sets autorestart=true for both processes
supervisord.conf redirects stdout/stderr to /dev/stdout for Docker logging

userStories.notes: CRITICAL: Read apps/agent-api/package.json to check for workspace dependencies (like @vibey/api-shared). If the agent-api imports from workspace packages, those must be available during the build stage. The OpenClaw base image (ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:main) already includes Node.js 22 and the OpenClaw runtime. Verify the exact command to start OpenClaw gateway from the Docker docs (https://docs.openclaw.ai/install/docker) — it might be 'node dist/index.js' or a custom binary. The supervisord.conf must handle process startup order: OpenClaw gateway should start first, then agent-api (since agent-api connects to the gateway).
